5f471d64cfd2e7763934df0a.applies_when: Your product idea touches regulated categories or you are unsure whether claims, labelling or testing rules apply.
conditions: The source's example product had few restrictions, which is category-specific and not a general finding.
This card flags the need for research; it does not substitute for qualified regulatory or legal advice.

090e016603b66024bad09bab.applies_when: You have completed the sixteen validation questions and need to make a go/no-go call or justify one to a partner.
conditions: The source does not provide a scoring formula; it deliberately accepts unresolved red flags and relies on the operator's judgement.
A strong brand plan does not fix fundamentally thin unit economics in paid acquisition.

67d4800441983b7711c04a3e.applies_when: Configuring an ad-spy tool such as Get Hooked to find products that already have proven spend and scale behind them.
conditions: Tool interfaces and filter names change; verify the current Get Hooked layout before relying on exact labels.
The 14-day runtime and 50-active-ads thresholds are the presenter's heuristics, not guarantees of profitability.
Niche categories under-include relevant health ads, so manual keyword search is often necessary.

cccca902b3896ea85b116184.applies_when: Screening candidate products before spending on creative, site build or inventory, especially in health and wellness.
conditions: Applies to physical problem-solution goods aimed at older buyers; not a universal test for all ecommerce categories.
Retail absence is a margin/protection heuristic, not proof of demand — validate separately with ad intelligence.
The source presents these as his screen, not an empirically benchmarked rule.

484b2d31c6738cfb1a3810bb.applies_when: Sourcing product ideas and native-ad angles aimed at a 60+ audience outside of ad spy tools.
conditions: Works specifically because older audiences dominate these sites — it is a demographic-targeting tactic, not a general trend feed.
Traffic-estimate tools may show nothing for new or low-traffic stores; absence of data is not absence of demand but also not validation.
Many widgets show low-quality or repeated offers; expect to filter heavily.

1586541150e9443dde95077b.applies_when: Validating a shortlisted product and checking whether competitors are already running native-style image ads.
conditions: Ad Library does not expose the performance or engagement metrics a paid spy tool provides; run time is a proxy, not proof.
One week of activity is the presenter's heuristic.
Searching vague keywords produces a lot of irrelevant results and takes longer than filtered spy tools.

1c7e14118dbb3f388f18f769.applies_when: You have a validated product with a history of running ads and need a starting creative angle before building your own.
conditions: This is angle mining, not permission to copy creative assets; the source describes replicating the angle and avatar, not the production.
Longest-running ads may still be unprofitable — run time only proves continued spend, not positive ROAS.
In saturated categories (the source names neuropathy), the same angle alone may not be enough; deeper copy research is his stated edge.

d3641c6bc6a895056f9a3339.applies_when: Deciding where to spend product-research hours, particularly as a beginner without a trained dropshipping eye.
conditions: This is the presenter's opinion and is tied to his stated 2026 timeframe; platform behavior changes.
The criticism applies to learning quality and saturation, not to whether winning products exist on those platforms at all.
A trained eye is presented as a prerequisite for burner methods, so beginners are the group most disadvantaged by them.

c9b651f1b77d02397f2e6461.applies_when: Starting a new ecommerce product search, or when a previous product test failed and you're tempted to jump straight to product hunting.
conditions: 'Market first' is the presenter's opinion and framework, not a proven law; it does not remove the need for validation and a solid funnel.
The listed markets are his examples, not a guaranteed set — supplements in particular he calls challenging despite long-term potential.

1918017689b2a6ca1432071a.applies_when: You have picked a market and want a fast list of specific emotional problems to build products and offers around.
conditions: The exact models, prompt text and list quality decay quickly; verify what the current Claude interface and models actually produce.
The presenter's claim that each sub-niche contains multiple seven/eight-figure businesses is his assertion, not measured evidence.

2e6da11c04cce1bb152ececd.applies_when: You want Claude to research real competitor brands, active ads, angles and funnels instead of relying on its training data alone.
conditions: Exact UI paths and field names are high-decay — confirm them in both tools before relying on this sequence.
Get Hooked is described as a free trial; pricing and access may change.

b09a0ce6330611d7c148ebf8.applies_when: Claude is connected to the Get Hooked MCP and you have narrowed to five emotional sub-niches.
conditions: The hour-long claim is the presenter's experience, not a benchmark.
Qualifying criteria come from active ad volume, which can reflect budget or testing rather than proven profitability — validate separately.
The exact prompt contents are not fully reproduced in the source; reconstruct to fit your own sub-niches.

b37123cc93c740376239be36.applies_when: Validating whether brands surfaced by your ad-spy research are actually selling at scale.
conditions: These are rough estimates, not financials — the presenter states plainly he cannot calculate exact revenue.
Both conversion rate and AOV are assumptions; conservative inputs make the floor more trustworthy than an optimistic guess.
SimilarWeb visit figures are estimates and free-tier search limits apply.

cd8817fc79ec09c12aadd6d4.applies_when: Deciding whether a sourced product can support paid acquisition before committing to a test.
conditions: These are the presenter's rules of thumb for a specific ad-cost environment, not universal economics.
3x COGS with a $30 floor can conflict at low price points — a $12 product gives 3.6x but only ~$36 margin, while a $10 product at 3x yields only $20 margin and fails rule two.
Margins must also cover shipping, payment fees and refunds; the rules as stated only address ad costs.

2b0c86c591158d80a1d65843.applies_when: A product test underperforms and you're deciding whether to kill the product, fix creatives, or fix the funnel.
conditions: The 90% figure is the presenter's observation, not a measured statistic.
This is in scope as test-triage, but optimizing the ads themselves belongs to creative and media-buying work, and fixing the checkout belongs to storefront work.

f5d6e64a0e54c1b8015fcfca.applies_when: A US product test is unprofitable and you need to determine whether the ads, not the offer or product, are the constraint.
conditions: Thresholds are US-specific and will decay as ad costs change; treat them as directional.
The presenter explicitly says CPM targets are relative and have no fixed KPI — the $80 line is his rough guide, not a rule.

3b6e3ec9a71b85e99b03a8cd.applies_when: Ad metrics look acceptable but the product still isn't converting, or you need to locate friction between click and purchase.
conditions: These are the presenter's working benchmarks, not validated universal thresholds; they vary with price point and model.
ATC and checkout figures can be distorted by bot traffic or by traffic quality from the ad itself, so read the ad and funnel metrics together.

33a09eb2fe9d840b800f4141.applies_when: Scoping a product-research sprint, or setting expectations that finding the product is only one part of a profitable launch.
conditions: The source maps these boundaries as a module taxonomy; it does not argue paid media or creative are unimportant — the reverse.

f2b99dd64bbd6c21ebcc5f7d.applies_when: Starting any avatar or customer-research effort and deciding what unit of analysis to research and record.
conditions: Demographics can still be used for media buying or reach planning, but they do not explain the choice and should not be the avatar's core.
A job statement without a circumstance usually collapses back into a generic persona.

9662bde03a613a3b9775b37f.applies_when: When you need new job candidates rather than validation of existing assumptions or feature wishlists.
conditions: Feature-request surveys and focus groups asking what to add produce wishlists, not jobs; they miss the context that causes purchase.
Off-label use signals a possible job, but confirm it recurs before treating it as a segment.

da14b9693decc2a2d96b3c43.applies_when: When choosing what evidence to gather and when a data-driven team wants to substitute reports for direct research.
conditions: This is not a rejection of analytics; it is a warning about using convenient operational data to answer causal questions.
Small qualitative samples can reveal a job but cannot establish its prevalence without follow-up measurement.

d60553248611613472cd3b85.applies_when: When diagnosing why prospects stall or abandon, or when building objection-handling into an avatar record.
conditions: Addressing objections on the page belongs to landing-page and offer work; this section only discovers and documents them.
Strong anxiety is not the same as low desire; a customer can want the progress and still not switch.

da4191b7964a57497bab771b.applies_when: Running customer interviews to uncover the job and the trigger moment behind a purchase.
conditions: Retrospective accounts are imperfect; ask for concrete events and sequences to reduce post-hoc rationalization.
Do not lead the customer toward the answer you want; let the timeline reveal the cause.

ec89bc0904f5b2f4d5ec2146.applies_when: When diagnosing whether problems sit in acquisition or in onboarding, activation and repeat usage.
conditions: Confusing the two produces avatars that explain acquisition but not retention, or vice versa.
A strong Big Hire can mask a broken Little Hire for months before churn shows up.

e30632499b68d270843cdb3a.applies_when: After a job is identified, when translating it into requirements for product, offer or messaging.
conditions: A spec describes experiences, not a feature list; converting it into features is product work that follows.
The spec changes when the circumstance changes, so re-check it against new interview evidence.

63c8da8b3648b60248f24581.applies_when: Synthesizing interview material into a shared internal view of the job before writing avatar records or messaging.
conditions: The storyboard is a synthesis artifact, not a substitute for raw quotes and evidence.
Resist smoothing the story into a tidy funnel; the messy path is where the insight lives.

294308de8309bca847b78784.applies_when: Writing or reviewing avatar records, especially when tempted to summarize without evidence.
conditions: Quotes can be edited for clarity but not for meaning; preserving the customer's phrasing is much of the value.
A single quote illustrates a job; it does not prove prevalence.

41ede02e56d13148680b3f41.applies_when: Planning avatar research and deciding how many distinct avatars to maintain.
conditions: No fixed number of avatars is universal; the right count depends on how many distinct jobs exist in your market.
Each retained avatar should carry the same evidence standard, so the set stays comparable.

37d2beb5692b4caf6d128344.applies_when: When hunting for new offers or messaging angles, especially in categories where customers complain about the process rather than the product.
conditions: Negative jobs still require a trigger to activate the purchase; discomfort alone does not cause switching.
Removing a task can reduce perceived value for some buyers who take pride in doing it themselves.

4a291c65cf40b93eaa0d9840.applies_when: When conversion is weak or customers describe long deliberation before buying.
conditions: The customer's mental competitive set often differs from the industry's own competitive map.
Doing nothing is frequently the strongest competitor and is easy to overlook.

e2bb9a4021c5abd9b4f747e9.applies_when: When your avatar or messaging lacks urgency and prospects agree with the message but never act.
conditions: Some categories have recurring triggers rather than one dramatic event; record the pattern, not a fabricated story.
Correlation between an event and purchase in one interview does not establish it as the general trigger.

058b163bd2aecafb34a577c2.applies_when: When prospects acknowledge the problem and the solution yet fail to switch.
conditions: More persuasive claims do not overcome a strong habit; friction removal usually matters more.
Some habits represent genuine preference and should be respected rather than attacked.

35de9821d18377bdcb01d3b9.applies_when: When the existing market is crowded and growth requires serving buyers the category has never reached.
conditions: Nonconsumers may be hard to recruit through normal customer channels; use referrals and community contexts.
Serving nonconsumers often requires rethinking the offer and the entry point, not just the message.

d6900a22a7ef609964f98620.applies_when: When reviewing support tickets, reviews or usage data and finding customers using the product in unexpected ways.
conditions: One creative customer is an anecdote, not a market; recurrence is the test.
Pursuing every unusual use fragments focus and can dilute the core job.

3f6f208703f16d88a3316595.applies_when: When reviewing existing persona documents or when a stakeholder asks for an age-and-income-based avatar template.
conditions: Demographic data still has legitimate uses in media buying, audience sizing and compliance; the objection is to using it as the causal explanation.
Fictional characters can be useful for communication and empathy, but only when built on real evidence rather than invented.

e8e9e127d97308d317087351.applies_when: When mapping the competitive set and understanding what switching away from a solution really costs the customer.
conditions: Customers may underreport what they fire out of politeness or loyalty; cross-check with the timeline.
In B2B contexts, firing a solution can involve relationships and politics beyond the product.

af8f9126927d63d81e2abdde.applies_when: Framing an innovation or product strategy, or when your team's data is descriptive (who buys, what they look like) but cannot predict which new offer will succeed.
conditions: Jobs Theory tells you why customers make choices and what to build; it does not tell you whether a job is ethical to serve (Christensen notes cigarettes can be hired to satisfy jobs but harm the customer — ethical judgment is separate).
A job is a highly specific construct, not a catchphrase for something a customer wants or needs; the loose use of 'jobs' as a buzzword defeats the purpose.
Christensen claims the odds of creating exactly the right product even when a firm intends to disrupt are probably less than 25% 'if that' — presented as his estimate, not a measured benchmark.
Identifying the job is only the beginning; you still need to design the accompanying experiences and integrate internal capabilities, or the insight does not convert to advantage.

c8f28fdc6c65028a4f29b211.applies_when: Designing customer research for a product with flat or declining sales, or when survey feedback ('cheaper, chunkier, chewier') is producing changes that don't move the number.
conditions: This is a case study of one chain's discovery, not a promised sales outcome.
Demographics did not separate the morning buyers — what they shared was a job, not a profile.
The afternoon job is inferred from Christensen's own experience as a father in line; it illustrates the reasoning rather than reporting measured sales.

ab9f2f70e75c76d6233d11d4.applies_when: Building avatars, running win/loss or purchase interviews, or briefing an agency or researcher before qualitative fieldwork.
conditions: Attribute-focused interviews and direct feature requests are the failure mode this method is designed to replace — they tell you what people say they want, not why they chose.
A trigger moment and a job statement are presented as the minimum baseline for any avatar; how many avatars you end up with is not fixed by the method.

69702437d033bc4467880726.applies_when: Diagnosing why prospects stall mid-funnel, or structuring interview notes and avatar definitions around what actually triggered and blocked a switch.
conditions: The four forces are a diagnostic frame for the decision, not a scoring model with published weights.

b5a6783a503a7ac85384fd51.applies_when: Auditing an existing avatar or persona deck, or approving a research brief, to check it is built on causal evidence rather than demographics.
conditions: The method is presented as universal, so the minimum requirements (evidence, trigger, job statement) apply to any avatar set; the number of avatars is explicitly not universal.
Christensen's own illustration: his age, height, shoe size and suburb did not cause him to buy the New York Times. Attributes can correlate with purchase propensity without causing it.
Correlation-based data is comfortable and makes managers sleep at night, which is why the fallacy is hard to shake — knowing it is a fallacy is not the same as acting on the difference.

6102e2da849e4faee6097c37.applies_when: When a dashboard of demographics, market share and CSAT is being used as the basis for a product or growth decision.
conditions: Christensen's framing of the data problem is an argument about explanatory power for innovation, not a claim that operations data has no value for running the business.
The 'less than 25%' odds figure is his estimate for hitting the right product, not a documented statistic from the sources cited.

ba25422e25e443ae4db4cb75.applies_when: When a roadmap item or landing page is being designed to 'work for everyone', or when multiple jobs are being averaged into a single offer.
conditions: This is an analogy from military procurement borrowed from Todd Rose's The End of Average; it is illustrative, not an ecommerce experiment.
It does not follow that every product must be customised — the lesson is against averaging incompatible jobs, not against standardisation.

a73e6aa41bc47029e6450bbb.applies_when: Doing competitive analysis, sizing an opportunity, or repositioning a product that looks like a commodity inside its own category.
conditions: Christensen admits he and his daughter may not have identified all the substitutes correctly that day — the exercise is directional.

The Unilever episode is a negative case: the executives present were not moved by the reframe and the firm continued differentiating in traditional ways, with margarine later declining in US households amid trans-fat health concerns. The outcome is presented as an outsider's observation about a counterfactual, not proof that this lens would have saved the business.
Jobs Theory clarifies why customers choose, not whether the solution is good for them — trans-fat and ethical questions sit outside the theory.

d231e21ff58f7563bb06a360.applies_when: Choosing the strategic frame for an innovation programme, or when a disruption lens has identified a threat but produced no product roadmap.
conditions: Christensen's claim that a well-defined job was implicitly at the core of most historic innovation successes is his belief, and he warns against relying on retrospective explanation — the value is in prediction.
This is theory framing from a 2016 book; treat the named company trajectories as examples at a point in time.

395c7d25ebcdca4272b24796.applies_when: Post-mortems where leadership failure is the assumed explanation, or when building an innovation process that you expect to produce breakthroughs.
conditions: The poll, spend and satisfaction figures are cited from period sources (McKinsey; strategy+business, 2015) and describe that period, not current benchmarks.
The DEC 'stupid manager' critique is an argument about structural causes, not a denial that management matters.

1f4f02b0b6ad3bdbf79edc84.applies_when: Generating job hypotheses in a workshop before doing timeline interviews, or mapping where an offer might fit into a customer's day.
conditions: These are illustrative examples from the book, not a taxonomy with operational thresholds.

dc943dfef7767cbee1f9605b.applies_when: Planning what happens after a jobs insight is validated — turning it into a blueprint, an experience and internal process change.
conditions: Presented as the authors' framework across chapters 6 to 8; the specifics of implementation are not detailed in this section.
Christensen's claim that experiences are harder to copy than products is a strategic argument, not an experimental result.

882242897d3b56c1145e9a58.applies_when: When framing a new product, offer or campaign and you need to state clearly what the customer is actually trying to accomplish rather than describing features or audience demographics.
conditions: A job is discovered, not created; the underlying job endures even as solutions change.
Jobs are fragile, story-like insights: breaking them into binary segments (male/female, new/existing) destroys meaning.

cb4347c65db15c7693505e0f.applies_when: When you need to flesh out a job for messaging, product design or an interview guide and the usual demographic or needs-based descriptions feel empty.
conditions: The answers are rich in context and resist spreadsheet breakdown; cluster them into a coherent story rather than segmenting further.

554e0cd99c6cc38837bb9cb7.applies_when: When assessing competitors, setting positioning, or feeling that your market is a zero-sum fight among near-identical products.
conditions: Working out the true job can take sustained effort and goes against habits built around product-attribute or demographic framing.
Do not assume the new framing makes you win; it only reveals who you must beat.

98d43a5458970b4486a9237a.applies_when: When a product or campaign built around an important-sounding need or a trend has stalled, or when reviewing an innovation brief that lacks circumstantial detail.
conditions: Needs and trends are not wrong, just insufficient for predicting choice on their own.

63b48fdec02e409d2ae99b90.applies_when: When approving a new product, channel or market entry, or when projections look attractive but rest on untested beliefs.
conditions: The source presents this as a complement to Jobs Theory, not a replacement for having a causal theory of customer choice.

53d529b9c994d90a8080723b.applies_when: When deciding whether to run a jobs-based research project or whether another method (efficiency analysis, price modelling) is the better tool.
conditions: Cost or efficiency is explicitly not a core element of a job, so don't force a jobs frame onto a purely economic decision.

a142b390da6f412d05f39cf9.applies_when: When diagnosing an innovation problem, teaching a team to reason about customer choice, or when results from industry best practices are inconsistent.
conditions: This is a management-practice argument from the source; theory still needs testing and refinement in your own context.
Prioritise different theories by the problem at hand rather than applying jobs theory to everything.

4a1389cd61ebce746ec1c0fd.applies_when: When reviewing an innovation or marketing brief and deciding whether the framing is likely to predict customer choice.
conditions: Jobs theory does not replace segmentation for execution purposes; it changes what the primary unit of innovation work is.

ecb46611592cda13875be6da.applies_when: When a repeatable process (fulfilment, creative production, onboarding) keeps producing errors that get patched rather than prevented.
conditions: The automotive quality story is used here as an analogy for innovation, not as an ecommerce case with measured results.
The source explicitly says innovation is still in a 'pre-quality revolution' state, so do not overstate how far this transfers.

1b89dfa3709a966469896959.applies_when: When outcomes are consistently poor or unpredictable and the reflex is to add patching steps rather than redesign the process.
conditions: The historical account is descriptive; it does not guarantee the same cost trajectory in other industries.

113a77a889664f5de9f8723a.applies_when: When your category looks saturated and growth has stalled under a one-size-fits-all offer aimed at the 'average' customer.
conditions: SNHU's revenue growth figures (about $535m by fiscal 2016; 34% compounded annual growth over six years) are case results, not promises.
The source notes the online division earned a modest $32m before the reframing and succeeded somewhat despite, not because of, existing processes.

a197e843c9cc17f3b39fcb1a.applies_when: When designing a landing page, tour or sales conversation and deciding which elements actually drive the decision.
conditions: This is a qualitative read from one university example; verify with your own prospect conversations before rebuilding a funnel.

2a7279282866d81bda8cafd6.applies_when: When your strategic plan assumes growth must come from taking share from direct rivals in a fixed market.
conditions: Strategic repositioning examples from BMW, Ford and GM are illustrations from the source, not verified outcomes for ecommerce.

06f039bfa4ba96477d867545.applies_when: When evaluating a new technology or channel and wondering whether it changes the customer's need or just the means of solving it.
conditions: Don't read this as an argument to ignore new technology; the source says new technology can improve how a job is solved.

6bfe4de638dc1f106cfa28e4.applies_when: When moving from research findings to designing the full customer experience, including post-purchase and service layers.
conditions: This is a claim about defensibility from the authors; it assumes deep integration, not a single added feature.

24843873732adbd78ba49c4f.applies_when: When preparing a strategy review, onboarding a team, or stress-testing a positioning statement.
conditions: These are diagnostic prompts, not a measurement instrument; pair them with evidence from customers.

184aad3cbf8bc44a12a12345.applies_when: You have multiple customer types (e.g., first-time buyers vs. repeat bulk buyers) receiving the same onboarding, offers or support flow and growth has stalled.
conditions: SNHU's growth (75,000+ online students, 10% surpluses, no tuition increases in four years) is a case example, not a benchmark you can copy.
Serving one job well may require deliberate de-prioritization of another segment — a strategic trade-off, not a free win.

a08d84e7c35c46de37d05e4f.applies_when: You need an innovation hypothesis and have no budget for formal research, or you're a founder/operator building for a market you personally belong to.
conditions: The Walkman example is retrospective and often cited selectively; ignoring research is survivorship-biased and not a recommended default.
A job that matters to you may still be too niche to build a business on without testing demand.

99ef75b0fbb2dd7f5c9638a9.applies_when: Your category looks mature, saturated or price-competitive, and you suspect existing market-size data can't see untapped demand.
conditions: Nonconsumption is invisible in current sales data; you must deliberately look for it.
The Depend figures are the company's own research and a single launch's results, not a general benchmark.

d9081272b7ddf77f6bb37b29.applies_when: You're scanning for unmet needs and notice customers jury-rigging spreadsheets, manual processes or odd substitutes.
conditions: Workarounds don't guarantee willingness to buy — validate that customers will pay for removed effort or anxiety.
QuickBooks' pricing/feature trade-off is a specific case, not a formula for pricing.

817a338fa0e1be68c7353725.applies_when: You're evaluating service design, flow simplification or any category where customers tolerate a painful routine.
conditions: Negative jobs in regulated categories (health, finance) may require new operational or legal structures, not just UX changes.
The MinuteClinic growth figures are a case illustration, not a forecast.

7da672f7f3e928cae8c1780e.applies_when: You have a long-established product, flat growth, and suspect you're defined by a category rather than by what customers are doing with it.
conditions: Non-medical off-label use can carry regulatory and safety risk; ZzzQuil required reformulating, not just marketing.
Single-brand revenue split figures are illustrative, not a target.

77824367b06d2ce8ddd16ae8.applies_when: You sell to a functional buyer (HR, L&D, IT, marketing ops) whose internal credibility depends on connecting your product to executive priorities.
conditions: FranklinCovey's revenue path ($589M peak in 2000, $130M in 2009, $220M in 2015) is a turnaround case example, not a template.
Owning outcomes requires delivery capacity; a subscription model fails if the customer's arising job isn't actually served.

d064d50c8bc46a635033a439.applies_when: You have traffic but poor conversion, or focus groups keep returning feature requests that don't move sales.
conditions: Growth and cancellation figures come from one Detroit-area builder in a distressed market; treat as a case example.
Timeline interviews require interpretation; a single dramatic quote is not proof of the pattern.

99cbc996163f6a0de02262fb.applies_when: You already have personas, focus groups, panels and competitive analysis but they don't produce clear innovation direction.
conditions: Jobs-based segments often don't align with your existing reporting segments, which creates internal friction.
The approach doesn't supply validated market size on its own; existing data may still miss nonconsumption.

5feb1dd866c8351fee1b5571.applies_when: Running a positioning, offer or roadmap review and needing a structured set of challenge questions.
conditions: These questions surface hypotheses; each still needs testing with real customers and purchase behavior.
The nonconsumption framing is the authors' theory, and job-based segmentation may conflict with how your business is currently organized and measured.

18af7f1a8bb64e620d6a69ef.applies_when: You are sizing a market, prioritizing a roadmap, or suspect your category definition is hiding demand (e.g., an ecommerce brand defining itself by product type instead of the progress customers want).
conditions: Reframing does not guarantee a large market; the job must have enough magnitude to change behavior.
The Pampers China outcome (approx. $1.6B and ~30% share by 2013) is a reported case result, not a benchmark.

74ac1061a1c9e97bf4d08833.applies_when: You are defining requirements for a product, page, or experience and want to avoid the common trap of solving only the functional dimension.
conditions: The source attributes the 'don't separate the three dimensions' insight to P&G's David Goulait; it is presented as his conversion, not a universal law.
Emotional/social weight varies by circumstance; don't assume it always dominates.

8d9e87b0a8afccb2ecd9a9a6.applies_when: You are gathering requirements from internal stakeholders, power users, or customers via interviews and need to validate that stated needs match real behavior.
conditions: This is the source's opinion (voiced via Intermountain's Todd Dunn) that 'you can't do design requirements in a conference room.' Apply with judgment for your context.
For ecommerce, transfer the technique as observing real browsing/checkout behavior and customer support context rather than assuming stated preferences.

1cd731e1d547b169cbe66a28.applies_when: Your growth has plateaued with current customers and you want to find new demand outside your existing base.
conditions: The book states most companies over-invest in studying current customers; nonconsumers are the underused source, not a replacement.
Workarounds signal opportunity but not guaranteed willingness to switch.

16f58e3ab9521192a31c3591.applies_when: You are measuring product-market fit, retention, or why downloads/purchases don't translate into repeat use.
conditions: Sales/marketing data commonly reflects only the Big Hire; supplement with consumption data.
Whether a product is 'doing a good job' depends on the customer's ongoing behavior, which single-point data can't show.

188ed2166ca729cb032ff0e7.applies_when: You are designing for conversion or adoption and want to reduce friction, not just add appeal.
conditions: Loss aversion 'twice as powerful' is attributed to Kahneman and Tversky, not this book's original claim.
The formula 'pull > inertia + anxiety' is a conceptual model, not a measurable equation.

e9fd545cfc4557210631bc60.applies_when: You have a strong offer but adoption/checkout is stalling, or you are launching a new or trust-sensitive product type.
conditions: These are the source's illustrations; the 'annual contracts prevent joining' point is framed as the industry 'coming around to the idea,' i.e., an evolving view.
Reassurance must be credible; a physical café that can't do banking is a brand signal, not a service.

4171f8999a9714cf69f20515.applies_when: You are launching or repositioning and need to understand the real competition and switching cost.
conditions: Customers are reluctant to fire anything until sure something is better, even when firing an imperfect solution.
Applies in B2B too — the source notes procurement decisions still carry emotional/social weight (e.g., a plant manager's career anxiety, a project manager's need to look competent).

df9261a8fe1bfb7ef6995de9.applies_when: You need to convert interview or observation notes into a structured narrative of a decision, or design an onboarding/purchase experience around real moments.
conditions: The Airbnb 45-storyboards detail is a reported example, not a required number.
Storyboarding is a tool to organize the struggle; it is not itself the research.

bd5e6104db6d0b8b72284d41.applies_when: You are interviewing recent buyers/purchasers to understand why they really chose you, and standard feature-preference surveys aren't giving usable answers.
conditions: The mattress transcript is explicitly NOT a prototype for all customer-research interviews; it is one illustration of depth.
The ambling, painstaking deficit-gathering is intentional but not suitable as a universal template.

7e2dead0b7e5ee1987282793.applies_when: You want a concrete model of how an apparently simple, impulse-looking purchase conceals a long, complex job when you gather circumstances.
conditions: This is a single retrospective interview; treat as an illustrative pattern, not statistical evidence.
The transcript is edited for length; details may be incomplete.

081951aa23227935b5282350.applies_when: You are mining customer behavior or support data and want to spot jobs you aren't currently designing for.
conditions: Unusual use can also indicate misuse or a different segment; investigate before designing for it.
The source frames this as a source of insight, not a proven method with fixed steps.

304df7bf3bc7975ba291a04e.applies_when: You are stuck for insight or want a low-cost way to start identifying jobs without launching a full research program.
conditions: Personal insight is a starting point; the source still recommends observation of others and nonconsumers.
The trap of only tweaking an existing product is a caution, not a prohibition.

25b3b4da19172824457e2c2d.applies_when: You are framing an innovation or experimentation program and want to argue for hypothesis-driven search over hoping for a lucky find.
conditions: This is the author's framing/opinion, not an empirically proven law.
The book claims no black box, but the cases it cites are selected successes and may suffer survivorship bias.

741dd2ac873ad5f73e3e17b7.applies_when: You have a strong niche offer and are tempted to broaden messaging to grab more buyers, or you're getting mismatched customers who churn or complain.
conditions: This is the source's opinion and depends on having a defined target job.
Over-signaling can unnecessarily shrink your market; calibrate to where mismatched hires cause real harm.

488785e75dab108b22d3636e.applies_when: You sell to businesses/teams and are tempted to treat the purchase as purely rational or functional.
conditions: The Mercer Pension Risk Exchange results (launched in US, UK, Canada; part of growth strategy) are reported case outcomes, not guarantees.
Transfer this reasoning to ecommerce only where you sell to professional buyers who carry personal accountability (e.g., B2B wholesale, team tools).

62392bd3a8d0dabfe84939e5.applies_when: Your team is stuck arguing whether a feature, page, or offer is 'good enough' and the debate keeps cycling.
conditions: The reframing is attributed to Chris Spiek of the Re-Wired Group, and is presented as his approach/knowledge.
Still requires a well-defined job; without one the reframed question is equally vague.

e5b43e1bd5d6458706360a4e.applies_when: Evaluating why a product sells but churns, or why purchase data looks healthy while usage or retention lags
conditions: Based on a single customer interview in the source; the authors explicitly say jobs discovery is about clustering insights, not one eureka.

355b8d9aca5c218042eaa0a9.applies_when: Designing qualitative customer research, mapping a purchase journey or choosing which friction to remove first
conditions: The four-force framing is the authors' Jobs Theory model, not a validated scoring system.
Barrier examples come from a single mattress interview and are hypotheses to test, not proven levers.

c4d6dd183e5b7337fd3446f7.applies_when: Designing qualitative research, deciding between a survey and interviews, or when quantitative data shows patterns without explaining them
conditions: Qualitative depth does not replace statistical validation of a hypothesis once it is formed.

fddf696158268e9e2a80d3c5.applies_when: Moving from customer research to product, offer or experience design for a new or repositioned product
conditions: The source presents this as a framework, not a template with fixed fields; adapt the dimensions to the category.

c5a5b09699384e8136a07a87.applies_when: Doing competitive analysis, category positioning or identifying barriers to adoption in a low-penetration market
conditions: Medtronic's results are a case example, not a promise; the source reports screening, counselling and treatment counts under one programme.
Barrier sets are market-specific and must be re-researched for each geography.

f45664fa39fe46b1f769bbed.applies_when: Differentiating in a category where features are easily copied, or justifying a premium price
conditions: The premium-price argument is the authors' interpretation, illustrated with cases such as IKEA, Uber and American Girl; it is not a tested formula for any specific category.

37a8c1976bae535f8486a3fe.applies_when: Reconsidering audience segmentation, store or site structure, or how to defend against copycat competitors
conditions: Job-based reorganisation is a strategic claim from the authors, illustrated with IKEA and American Girl, not a repeatable step-by-step process.

2174f296edbef2890dfdfcf3.applies_when: Reducing pre-purchase hesitation on considered purchases such as furniture, mattresses or high-ticket items
conditions: These are hypotheses generated from a single interview in the source, not validated programme results.

54181849803366b06cb9aa77.applies_when: Optimising product pages, managing marketplace reputation, or deciding what review content to surface
conditions: The 95/86/one-third figures are cited from external research in the source and are dated; validate against current data for your category.

2b63dd9f725fe6caf54eeaaa.applies_when: Developing brand positioning, naming a product line, or deciding whether to extend a brand into new categories
conditions: Purpose-brand claims and the 80 percent share figure for Milwaukee are presented by the authors and are not independently evidenced in the text.

d125c1d8df510577bc55c5fe.applies_when: Reviewing a research plan that relies mainly on doctor or expert panels, feature-preference surveys or disease/behaviour statistics
conditions: Based on a medical-device case; principles transfer to considered ecommerce purchases but specific numbers do not.

95dea7e97e723e850d7148c2.applies_when: Deciding whether a research finding is a real insight worth building on or just an interesting data point
conditions: Feeling true is a subjective signal, not validation; the source pairs it with continued research and clustered interviews.

f13714393d433b660506d09c.applies_when: Turning qualitative job research into a prioritised roadmap of experiments for a retailer or brand
conditions: All hypotheses in the source derive from one interview and are explicitly framed as starting points.

7b4b73b27c3187fb04daae3a.applies_when: Reconciling an existing design-thinking or human-centred design process with jobs-based research
conditions: This is a positioning observation by the authors about their own theory, not an empirical comparison of methods.

1da34b764041251699108b76.applies_when: Deciding brand positioning or evaluating whether feature/benefit expansion is diluting what the brand stands for
conditions: Brand status is hard to regain once lost; the source treats Volvo's post-1999 shift toward flashier cars as a cautionary case where a safety purpose brand weakened and recovery was slow.
The 'ultimate competitive advantage' framing is the source's strong claim, not a guaranteed outcome.

88dec6a091ff0d86bd40fd59.applies_when: After customer research has surfaced a job and you need to translate it into requirements for a product, service or experience
conditions: A job is rich and complex; a thin or purely functional spec will produce a solution that misses what customers actually need.
The source insists solutions must be complete, meaning core product plus purchase and use experiences; a good product alone is not enough.

b1a2c52e24c1c41bca39aa7b.applies_when: When your product is strong but customers still struggle to buy, onboard or get value from it
conditions: This is a design principle, not a claim that every company must literally sell a subscription or service.
The source's examples come from healthcare, automotive and education; the transfer to ecommerce is that checkout, delivery, onboarding and support all count as part of the solution.

59d7dc3a768a670402a290c8.applies_when: When restructuring seems like the answer to growth or execution problems, or when functions deliver in silos
conditions: The source explicitly says large-scale reorgs are usually not practical and traditional structures have value; this is not a call to abolish functions.
Building job-centered processes is described as very hard and slow, not a quick fix.

e5fa6414f83eac0d311c370c.applies_when: When customers abandon or stall because of friction such as paperwork, coordination or repeated follow-up
conditions: The SNHU results are a case example, not a guaranteed return for other businesses.
Removing customer complexity usually raises internal cost and process intensity; the source argues this pays off through acquisition and premium pricing, but that tradeoff should be tested.

c79827d20a3fbe5a1723cea0.applies_when: When dashboards full of conversion, retention or cost metrics don't explain whether customers are actually succeeding
conditions: Internal revenue metrics can mislead: the source describes Intuit forcing trial users to register by phone to enable upsells, which created friction and focused people on revenue rather than the customer benefit.
Customer-benefit measurement is described as genuinely hard and not automatically available from systems.

f8563f7ac475f8069b37f099.applies_when: When process improvement, automation or cost reduction is underway and you need a criterion beyond throughput
conditions: The source's point is that textbook process optimization is insufficient, not that efficiency is unimportant.
Flexibility has costs; the claim is that job attachment justifies them when the job is well understood.

a68b90c9abdaab38845edc87.applies_when: When scaling operations across regions, product lines or channels and each team reinvents the same steps
conditions: The source presents this as a principle imported from software engineering, illustrated by Amazon, not as a universal implementation recipe.
Modular reuse can conflict with local adaptation; the alignment with the job is the tie-breaker.

9246aff2271c56858744428b.applies_when: Kicking off a new product, feature or service, especially when engineering or channel ownership is fragmented
conditions: The press release is a framing device, not a substitute for customer research into the job.
The source does not describe the full Amazon document or approval process; treat details beyond the framing as outside the source.

b28cb75bb455fdf086dc8ff8.applies_when: When customers experience a broken journey across handoffs and each function believes it is doing its job
conditions: This does not require a full reorganization; the source says stewardship can be achieved through processes, metrics and culture.
The Mayo and ICU cases are healthcare examples; in ecommerce the transferable idea is owning the end-to-end job journey across teams.

41516283a4bcdc9d6bf7097d.applies_when: When cross-functional teams argue from their own professional backgrounds instead of solving the customer's problem
conditions: This is drawn from the CFPB setup under Elizabeth Warren, a regulatory context; the transferable mechanism is the job-focused meeting, not the specific divisional structure.
The source warns of a typical DC paralysis risk that the job focus was designed to avoid.

4ff2f07c0d04e0627c62eb12.applies_when: When considering a product extension or new service built on your existing technology or supply strength
conditions: The restaurant failure figure is the source's illustration, not a claim about your market.
The source frames stack fallacy as highlighting the same hazard as Jobs Theory, not as a rigorous predictive model.

f77af3bfce88f10d3bec6977.applies_when: When your product has many features but customers churn because they don't need most of them
conditions: The source attributes OnStar's ultimate success to this job focus and to process innovation, not to the features it launched with.
Listening to calls is described as revealing and uncomfortable work, not a one-off survey.

7afa986236c849779348ea68.applies_when: When a growing organization is making decisions from data and internal assumptions rather than customer contact
conditions: The source does not prescribe a research cadence or sample size; it argues for repeated direct exposure as the company grows.
Attribution here is the source's interpretation; it is not an experimentally validated rule.

b64e6ebef5d1aa785302c54c.applies_when: When your product depends on rapidly improving technology embedded in a slow-moving hardware, channel or regulatory environment
conditions: This required going outside the normal approval and validation sequence, described as very hard in an established organization.
The competitive advantage came from the process set as much as the product; simply owning the technology was not sufficient.

eb46568f92f146f7f83e21ea.applies_when: When a partner or channel is the front line of purchase and your offering is a small share of their revenue
conditions: The specific 20 percent and ten-dollar figures are from the source's OnStar example, not a general benchmark.
Channel incentives differ by market and contract structure; verify your own economics rather than copying these numbers.

8f4275d43e5ff0263ebdab6d.applies_when: When your category is vulnerable to budget cuts because clients see it as a discretionary product purchase
conditions: The source reports FranklinCovey doubled revenue and increased profit tenfold over six years, but this is a case example, not a forecast for other firms.
Taking responsibility for outcomes increases scope and risk compared with selling a bounded product.

9b78a943561e752c69dd6dc5.applies_when: When a research-backed improvement keeps dying in implementation despite good evidence
conditions: The milkshake example ended in a quiet death of the idea; the source uses it to show how internal forces defeat good ideas, not to claim all process changes fail.
Deming's line that if you can't describe what you are doing as a process then you don't know what you are doing is the source's framing, not an operational rule.

b8edb10a0fa1cb243f20bf4b.applies_when: Reviewing a product line, customer journey or growth plan against the job you believe you are hired for
conditions: These are diagnostic questions from the source, not a validated scoring instrument.
Answers will be organization-specific; the exercise is meant to surface misalignment, not produce a benchmark.

e95a35c04ebc115782e805ef.applies_when: Diagnosing why a once jobs-focused ecommerce brand now chases product lines, channel metrics or exec pet projects instead of customer progress.
conditions: The fallacies describe tendencies in the authors' research and experience, not a measured law; treat as diagnostic lenses.
The V8 case (sales quadrupled in under a year after re-framing against vegetables) is a single anecdote, not a benchmark or promise.

Reorganizations are usually impractical; the authors recommend embedding jobs focus in processes, metrics and culture over time rather than large reorgs. A cited 2010 Bain study of 57 major reorganizations found fewer than one-third produced meaningful performance improvement.

241ce7605df037a373936ec1.applies_when: Setting up research cadence and decision rights so customer-job evidence survives contact with the operating dashboard.
conditions: Passive data is qualitative and context-dependent; it is directionally helpful, not objective reality, and will not survive being reduced to a single KPI.
The authors' argument that no customer has a job called 'I need to spend a couple of hours at the store' is an assertion about retail, not a general law.

4f376b72845abb56d20c8f5a.applies_when: Evaluating catalog expansion, brand extension, line extensions or acquisition of adjacent product lines before committing.
conditions: This does not forbid any expansion; it warns that expansion without a job rationale confuses customers and invites focused disrupters.

The V8 line proliferation (Spicy Hot, Lemon, Picante, Roasted Chicken, Low-sodium, Organic, Splash, V-Fusion + Tea) is the authors' illustrative example of lost clarity, not a measured failure of any specific flavor.

39e7eece8ab97e6a0bdfb3bf.applies_when: Running innovation, range or investment reviews where sales, marketing, product and finance all present supporting numbers.
conditions: This is a critique of decision process, not a claim that quantitative data is worthless — the point is that all data is man-made and embeds choices.
Psychological dissonance-avoidance is offered as an explanation of the pattern, not a tested organizational law.

6c8e591b96b4159133875a9b.applies_when: Choosing or defending a data source for a positioning or product decision, or when a team treats dashboards as ground truth.
conditions: The authors still call search-trend data directionally helpful; the objection is to treating it as objective reality, not to using it at all.
The Bobby Kennedy GNP passage and the author's son's HBS section-leader story are illustrative arguments about unmeasured value, not research findings.

bdb72d8876723349a61ff78c.applies_when: When feature requests and backlog items pile up but no one can say which ones matter, or a core product step has become the optimization target itself.
conditions: The chapter-prefill result is a company experiment, not a published benchmark or guaranteed lift.
Full 'no interview' TurboTax is described as years away; interim progress is still meaningful but incomplete.
Scott Cook frames the challenge of sustaining focus as an open question — 'the sixty-four-billion-dollar question' — rather than a solved management problem.

554792a99a93be397734c981.applies_when: Making the internal business case for adopting jobs-based language, or auditing which of the four benefits is actually missing.
conditions: The four categories are drawn from CEOs the authors interviewed, not from controlled study.
The authors acknowledge unanswered questions about how to keep teams consistently rallying around a hard goal; treat this as direction, not a complete operating system.

89759f0f168f42e90795e39f.applies_when: When a company has a mission or purpose statement that nobody can translate into product, service or merchandising decisions.
conditions: The Lifebuoy outcome is a company success story (one of the fastest-growing brands in the period described), not a controlled trial of the job-framing method.
Health behavior thresholds cited are as reported by the source; do not restate them as current medical guidance outside that context.

207a9f4cfe25a2f1319fd2c1.applies_when: Prioritizing a service, feature or benefit roadmap where everything looks technically feasible and marketable.
conditions: The fifteen-second decision was fast, but implementation was not — the source distinguishes deciding from executing and acknowledges imperfect workarounds.
OnStar's founding-CEO account is a single-company narrative, not evidence that any organization can replicate the autonomy.

583f1aa39218bc33b779cabb.applies_when: Cross-functional planning sessions where each department optimizes its own metrics and meetings end without alignment.
conditions: The claimed productivity impact is a leadership observation from the authors' interviews, not a measured effect size.
Simple language does not mean simple analysis; the difficulty of defining jobs accurately is stated explicitly.

9bd4037b7ab20fa402c8df4c.applies_when: Running a quarterly strategy or innovation review, or onboarding a new functional leader, to test alignment around customer progress.
conditions: These are the authors' diagnostic prompts, not a validated assessment instrument.
The process-over-reorg recommendation is a general argument; it does not guarantee culture change without sustained leadership attention.

e37c61237e0ef797a781eebd.applies_when: Teaching or re-anchoring a team on customer-centric framing before writing positioning, roadmaps or campaign briefs.
conditions: The 'no customer job to go to the store' claim is illustrative of the authors' framework, not an empirical finding about all retail.
The listed successes are examples chosen to illustrate job-centered organizing; their outcomes are not attributed to this framework alone.

51230f4f32c94165817c5fb5.applies_when: When an ecommerce team's roadmap or feature debates lack a shared anchor, or when employees need to make day-to-day tradeoffs without escalation.
conditions: The source presents this as observed pattern across several organizations, not a guaranteed outcome.
A vague job statement in adjectives ('be convenient') fails as a compass.
People whose work doesn't align with the job may need to be restructured or counseled out, per the Deseret News example.

0959208def437018e11bea6d.applies_when: When making the business case for job-based positioning, or when restructuring teams, budgets or KPIs around customer jobs.
conditions: The source describes these as benefits observed across successful organizations, not a guaranteed sequence.
Embedding jobs in culture is described as slow and effortful; expect resistance from parts of the organization.
Operational efficiency still matters — the source argues it is only value-creating when it serves a high-priority job.

2c9eb2206eeb60783afe9bbd.applies_when: When designing customer-service or support empowerment policies, or when deciding how much discretion front-line staff should have.
conditions: Examples are drawn from higher education (SNHU), not ecommerce; the transferable mechanism is discretion bounded by job clarity.
Unbounded discretion is not the claim — actions were still consistent with an explicit job.

1f1b2827cce21770cc58f07a.applies_when: When rewriting a company mission, vision or internal rallying cry so it actually guides decisions.
conditions: The source warns against generic mission statements but still says articulation requires real work and deep cultural embedding.
Shorthand rallying cries only work when the underlying job is genuinely understood.

21955247a148ccf55227e691.applies_when: When choosing KPIs or analytics dashboards for an ecommerce business, or when data is abundant but feels disconnected from customer value.
conditions: The source argues data reflects the biases of whoever chose what to collect and discard; treat internal metrics as models, not reality.
Hard-to-measure outcomes still matter profoundly; the 95% figure is an example from SNHU, not a benchmark.

9b38f4060bd27e435503f24b.applies_when: When designing monitoring and enforcement systems for a core customer promise such as price competitiveness or delivery speed.
conditions: This describes Amazon's system as reported by the authors; your margins, product set and competitor set differ — don't copy the threshold.
Requires reliable benchmark price data and automation; manual equivalents may not keep pace.
Check your local pricing and competition regulations before implementing automatic undercutting.

e04fb9d3213ce7e67a784441.applies_when: When an established product or channel is losing ground and you need to decide which jobs to double down on and which to abandon.
conditions: This is a strategic triage process, not a quick optimization; the Deseret News example took years and organizational change.
Abandoning a job can mean losing customers and staff who valued the old bundle.

782e3f599df414337c363ddd.applies_when: When writing positioning or creative strategy and the functional benefit alone doesn't explain customer attachment.
conditions: The Deseret News social growth figures (low millions to over 100 million followers through its FamilyShare Network) come from one organization's reported results and should be treated as an example, not a benchmark.
Emotional framing that doesn't match a real job is positioning decoration, not Jobs Theory.

6e6df56de0a97bbd1cabf584.applies_when: When demographic or psychographic segments aren't producing differentiated messaging, or when a promising audience seems 'unfindable' by standard targeting.
conditions: The 56% figure is one research finding about American news consumers, not a general benchmark.
Job-based segments may be invisible to standard ad targeting; you may need to reach them through behavior or interest signals instead.

336e01894bc3b15a42df13ff.applies_when: When a scaling ecommerce business's processes, org chart or reporting feel increasingly detached from what customers want.
conditions: Efficiency and process discipline are not the enemy — the source says functional oversight is a requirement of competitive markets.
This is a persistent structural drift, not a one-time fix; expect to re-audit as you grow.

b2121bd6e7ce12b5f16233cb.applies_when: When checking whether a job statement is genuinely a job, or when a team's 'job' is really a preference, a spec or an aspiration.
conditions: Setting the right level of abstraction is described as more art than science; expect iteration.
Jobs theory is bounded — applying 'job' to every human motivation dilutes its clarity and predictability.
The theory was built inductively and its author explicitly says anomalies are useful signals of its boundaries, not disproof.

d113ec3fa69f7dd555e08515.applies_when: You have a rough product or offer idea and need a fast sanity check on whether it can be profitable before investing in research or creation.
conditions: Company examples are the presenter's illustrations, not benchmarks.
The matrix is an estimation tool, not a demand-measurement instrument; quantitative search volume validation lives elsewhere.

c97ccae246066f6d736fb29a.applies_when: You are starting qualitative research on a new niche and need to see who already sells to this market and how they frame themselves.
conditions: This is a qualitative framing scan; it does not measure demand or traffic.
A competitor's existence and polish are signals to study, not proof you can win the same segment.

3e4fe752116bdff8b05536bf.applies_when: Analyzing competitor landing pages or sales copy to infer what kind of buyer each promise is written for.
conditions: The source's inference about a given buyer's psychology is interpretation of copy, not verified data.
A $60 price point and DVD format are examples from one case, not benchmarks to copy.

46eec728bb7e933c57cd1937.applies_when: You want to know what a category's existing books or products fail to deliver, so you can design around known shortcomings.
conditions: Reviews reflect a self-selected sample of buyers; the source also warns that some commenters are 'keyboard warriors' who consume programs without applying them.
Do not treat a single critical review as a mandate to change direction — the source says you cannot respond to every piece of feedback.

b08301158fb6bfe1530f48ed.applies_when: You are hunting for high-intent, self-aware prospects and want pain-point language they will recognize instantly.
conditions: A 100% never-tried-anything list is not necessarily worse; the source's claim is that failed-solution buyers are among the best, not the only good segment.
You still have to solve their actual problem; the source does not suggest exploiting past frustration.

6e03505404f77e2a777d111b.applies_when: You are choosing where to dig for psychological hurdles rather than tactical how-to answers.
conditions: The source's Reddit-versus-Quora split is the presenter's experience, not a platform rule; verify per category.
Online answers cannot be verified for identity or truthfulness; the source finds this limitation significant enough to justify primary interviews.

0017b1b018a48c98ca6413f1.applies_when: You have a pile of forum answers and need to convert them into avatar language and benefit angles.
conditions: Quoted benefits come from a fitness example; transfer the method, not the specific claims, to other categories.
Word frequency reflects who happens to post, not the whole market.

e2f0e8697fe794251c2cb1fd.applies_when: You have desk research and want to validate and deepen it with real conversations before building.
conditions: The source's volume claim (thousands of emails, hundreds of replies) is his scale, not a required benchmark.
Interviews and forum posts can both contain socially desirable answers; look for repeated patterns to reduce noise.

46a98b023ad345caede4feae.applies_when: You are mining reviews or forum threads and feel tempted to script, scrape, or summarize with an algorithm.
conditions: The 60–80% figure is the presenter's personal time allocation, not a universal rule.
Manual reading does not scale; the source accepts that trade-off deliberately and others may choose differently.

fcf1bd930a6c17081f79cad4.applies_when: You are reading critical reviews and trying to decide which complaints to act on.
conditions: The book and review details are illustrative examples, not proof that science depth causes purchase or non-purchase.
Choosing to ignore feedback can be wrong if the complaint is repeated across the target segment.

2ce06b2439fa00e5ae167587.applies_when: You are deciding whether a niche has commercial backing for a paid product or offer.
conditions: Competitor profitability is inferred from appearance in this method, not verified; treat it as a directional signal.
Price examples from the source are case illustrations, not recommended pricing.

0d27b0e8ba75b1073e814c57.applies_when: You are about to write ad copy, a VSL or a landing page and want to check whether you actually know who you are writing to.
conditions: The source's $10k/day framing comes from a paid-community marketer selling a drop-shipping course; treat scale claims as his positioning, not a benchmark.
Translating avatar language into hooks and scripts belongs in a later creative module; this card is only about the avatar definition.

d75e33882fdbba520995d561.applies_when: You have picked a demographic and need to build a real avatar without defaulting to AI-generated personas.
conditions: This is a manual-first protocol; the source still says AI tools like Gemini or Claude have unmatched efficiency and detail once you already understand your avatar.
The method is universal but the 80/20 forum-to-review split is the presenter's recommendation, not a measured law.

f1ca3f6fbc7043f47c651bba.applies_when: You are starting the forum half of a manual research sprint and need to find threads worth mining.
conditions: The source's specific example queries are for a cat kidney product and a hair-restoration product; substitute your own category's problem statements rather than copying them.
Search-engine behaviour and subreddit availability change, so verify what surfaces for your niche rather than assuming these exact queries still return the same threads.

3db1dccaa8da15feca563f58.applies_when: You are in a research session and need a repeatable way to capture material you can actually write from.
conditions: The source's advice to use the avatar's own words including insults is about authenticity, not about harassing customers; use judgement on what is ethical to reflect back.
Do not attribute a single Reddit comment to your whole audience; it is one data point, and the method relies on repetition across many threads.

dae729a4f6bbb2d6a64c499b.applies_when: You have raw research and need to decide the emotional register your ads should use.
conditions: Emotional register and claims must stay within ad-platform policies and honest representation; the source's vivid fear framing is a copy technique, not permission to exaggerate outcomes.
The source is describing a marketing course audience and a pet supplement example; verify the dominant emotion in your own niche rather than assuming it transfers.

326d0318ebcce1ec3c21cecf.applies_when: You are writing hooks or objection-handling copy and want to reference failed prior attempts credibly.
conditions: Named competitor or medical solutions should be referenced factually; do not invent efficacy comparisons the research does not support.
Price figures quoted by forum users are anecdotes, not verified market pricing.

301d338a9f16a862a81ad40b.applies_when: You are writing hook lines and want to avoid clever-but-empty angles that make the avatar roll their eyes.
conditions: The source's framing 'people buy when they feel understood' is his opinion, supported by example, not a measured conversion law.
Hook creation and script writing belong downstream in a creative module; this card covers only the understanding required before writing them.

4e2d70bdca59814ca3348f9c.applies_when: You are deciding whether to run deep-research prompts instead of doing forum and review mining yourself.
conditions: This is a strong opinion from a marketer who sells community access, and it is framed as a starting-out rule; experienced operators may get value from AI-assisted research with strong inputs.
The source does not claim manual research is superior to AI in efficiency or detail, only in building genuine understanding.

ef0ecef3dfbbbc8a8ff41853.applies_when: You are cataloguing research into avatar records or auditing whether an existing avatar is complete.
conditions: The source warns against persona templates with demographic fields and no job, such as '30+ year old woman with knee pain'; those should not count as avatars.
A quoted line from one forum user may not represent the whole demographic; consolidate multiple sources into the record.

5d6b9c23511aeff0b6405320.applies_when: You are deciding how much research effort to invest before spending on ads or scaling a proven offer.
conditions: The presenter is selling a drop-shipping course and community and uses $10,000 days as marketing framing; results are his example, not a promise for your account.
No specific spend, testing budget, timeframe or statistical benchmark is given, so do not treat the scale claims as a forecast.

de6f52d002316a301253302e.applies_when: You are drafting copy for a problem where some buyers are already confident and others are not.

f6f18000b06c6bdc53157ee5.applies_when: Diagnosing why creatives or offers aren't differentiating, or when starting avatar research from scratch.

912d3aa3c168fa60d22d9527.applies_when: Researching a health, hobby, or subculture niche where customers congregate and describe their situation in their own terms.

9b44ebb5a6e91cd3f06af2dd.applies_when: Writing ad copy and choosing channels for a specific cohort you're targeting.
conditions: The channel mapping (Facebook groups for older, TikTok for younger) is the source's illustrative example, not a validated demographic rule — verify against your own buyer data.

873f2122bf9147e2ebc47c2a.applies_when: Writing ads or landing pages for a researched avatar and converting objections into hooks.

a968d0d00a117a50011e14a5.applies_when: Positioning a commodity product against identical competitors, or when testing offers and framing.

c5efc108c9c95161a0da15a4.applies_when: Creating or auditing avatar documents, and onboarding writers or media buyers to them.

8ef3a86a513709e70e45d8ab.applies_when: Early niche or offer research when you need to discover the language and sub-topics your market actually searches for.
conditions: Autocomplete shows what people type, not how many people type it — you need a volume tool to judge size.

771e65508b21adf234e3c479.applies_when: After autocomplete mining, when you need to size demand, compare sub-topics, or check whether a niche has seasonal patterns.

Tool navigation is version-dependent; confirm current steps in Google Ads.

bb02448d1007c06d349cf317.applies_when: Validating that a niche has real buyers and harvesting market-tested language, after search-intent research on Google.

Review sentiment can be gamed or skewed by a small number of vocal buyers.

146bbf72ccfa362303ffde70.applies_when: Researching competitor messaging and offer angles in industries with active Meta advertising, after you have defined your avatar.

Requires ads to be publicly visible in the library; ad library coverage and interface details change and should be verified.

f33468b235557fdb8adb307e.applies_when: Designing a research plan or deciding how much weight to give survey-style stated preferences versus behavioural evidence.
conditions: Search intent still over-represents researchers versus buyers; it is an indication, not a guarantee of purchase.

32ce1018d3e230d34ead91f4.applies_when: Moving from raw avatar research into copy themes, ad angles and offer framing.

cef3f6a44c443f368c6ed72f.applies_when: You already have a customer base and are preparing a new offer, upsell or product line for that same market.
conditions: The 'top 20%' figure is the source's framing without a stated method for ranking customers — define your own ranking metric (revenue, repeat purchase, margin) and document it.

e6c10689be00d4948cef40b9.applies_when: Deciding which platforms to prioritise for content and campaigns based on your avatar's actual presence.
conditions: Demographic data sources vary in methodology and are usually revised; confirm figures from a current, credible source rather than relying on a single page.

826d0e12dcdab71f9afedb6b.applies_when: Planning campaign timing, seasonal pushes, or content scheduling around your avatar's routines and transitions.
conditions: Life-event research identifies correlation with buying windows, not proof that the event caused a purchase.

229a47af9d515aafa689458e.applies_when: Constructing an avatar document that will be handed to copywriters, media buyers or creative teams.
conditions: Psychographics are inferred from behaviour and interviews, so they are less reliable than demographic fields.
Geographic segmentation matters less for purely digital delivery but still affects channel and language choices.

0926a3def9d8225a48f0ec5f.applies_when: Scoping who does what when planning a launch so research outputs are not confused with execution deliverables.
conditions: These boundaries come from one internal operating model and may need adapting to small teams where one person covers several stages.
The research phase produces direction, not finished copy or media plans.

0ea951a84570123931e082ed.applies_when: Screening competitor ads in the Meta Ad Library and deciding which angles to model or test.
conditions: Duration can also reflect campaigns left running by neglect, always-on brand ads, or ads with low spend — the underlying assumption is the presenter's, not a measured fact.
Ad Library visibility and sorting behaviour can change; verify the current interface.
Only applies where competitors actually run ads on Meta.

e35f8fec52f0e1cfeeb1650d.applies_when: Writing the value proposition or offer copy after the Who, What, When and Where steps are complete.
conditions: Why-level motivations are interpretive and can be wrong; validate with purchase behaviour and customer conversations where possible.

0934edc554c3c5ac59414377.applies_when: You are sourcing or marketing a saturated dropshipping product (e.g., an AB stimulator) and deciding how to enter a market dominated by 7-figure brands.

b399ed19a017796620bccca9.applies_when: You need to know which demographics and desires incumbents already own before choosing an untapped avatar.
conditions: Access to tools that estimate ad spend or traffic (such as third-party ad spy software) can speed this up; verify current functionality before relying on it.

083c7052a4f04ef8ab849118.applies_when: After mapping the incumbent avatar, you want candidate buyer segments your product already serves but competitors ignore.

70b5dd026992d98a67f92bb6.applies_when: You have a candidate avatar from review mining and need evidence it is large and painful enough to justify a campaign.

208f632d3ddc68d580f4e136.applies_when: You are between discovery and deep research and need a structured starting input for an AI prompt or manual research.
conditions: Do not mistake the preliminary sketch for a finished avatar record; the value comes from the subsequent deep research.

be3576be73a2b7426063aa12.applies_when: You have prioritised one avatar and need comprehensive psychological and situational detail before writing copy.
conditions: The source found Gemini wider in depth of sources while ChatGPT was slightly less deep in his one comparison — this is a single-run observation, not a stable benchmark.

09f09782497ec80a4a46278b.applies_when: You have two or three candidate avatars and must pick one to build a campaign around.
conditions: An isolated avatar can be commercially thin; the source pairs this with a heavy proof requirement for exactly that reason.

2b67b2edcb1afddb012f5697.applies_when: You are finalising research to hand off to copywriting or creative development (the source routes writing to a separate copy module).

60a58f44e42def8ce6b172b1.applies_when: Deciding strategy at the start of marketing a product in a saturated or dropshipped category.

a1faffe601952ebdaa145ee5.applies_when: You or a colleague keep conflating TAM, ICP and persona, or campaign briefs lack a clear audience boundary before content planning.

6f9531c5c47375ee0e2e82c5.applies_when: You lack a documented ICP or persona and need raw customer language fast, or want the qualitative layer that surveys and CRM fields cannot provide.

ff3969ab7ccbc2dba810219e.applies_when: You are assembling ICP data and trying to work out where the evidence should come from for a specific company size.

ba49787189ec73a669a14bbb.applies_when: You have raw qualitative data and need to turn it into a tangible ICP or persona document for the team and tools.

Tool project features change; confirm current behavior in the LLM you use.

8cf79dbd3fd44e355348ee99.applies_when: You are planning content topics and there is disagreement about how deep or advanced the coverage should be.

834684cbb868445e41e0a59e.applies_when: You are building the ICP record and need to decide which fields belong to the account profile versus each buying-committee member.

af1c969a5868843af5c31cf3.applies_when: You are running Meta ads for a niche avatar and deciding whether to narrow the audience settings.

7a8d7aa38df0e559b24e7c1c.applies_when: Merchandising a commodity-like product category where shoppers can easily compare your SKU, price, and shipping terms with competitors.

e141a5bda4f3546be06e8afb.applies_when: Creating kits, gift sets, starter bundles, or subscription tiers to raise average order value without adding low-value fulfillment complexity.

0a29207c3138f45df2881e3c.applies_when: Writing return, satisfaction, fit, delivery, or product-support terms for a PDP, cart, or checkout where hesitation centers on wasting money.
conditions: Model return shipping, product disposition, fraud, and support costs before strengthening a guarantee.

264e18c4c7be8fbb9ab14fb9.applies_when: Deciding whether to add or expand a return, satisfaction, replacement, or make-good promise for an ecommerce product offer.
conditions: Do not use lead conversion or sales-call close-rate examples as if they were purchase-conversion benchmarks.

4fc1b785cdaa089190ebdbf7.applies_when: Planning a product drop, preorder, seasonal campaign, or time-bound bundle when customers tend to postpone a decision.
conditions: Repeatedly extended or fabricated deadlines undermine trust and may create compliance risk.

e456aab8c58ac3f398ca9f50.applies_when: Merchandising a limited product run, constrained seasonal inventory, made-to-order capacity, or first-buyer bonus during a launch.

966feb3ae826ba202e042160.applies_when: Naming a product kit, collection, seasonal promotion, subscription tier, or replenishment program for a specific customer use case.
conditions: Forcing all five elements into every name can create awkward, overly long titles.

511c3a0c4cf9e30365b7b86c.applies_when: Launching or changing a promotion, bundle, bonus, guarantee, or pricing structure across paid acquisition, storefront, checkout, and lifecycle email.
conditions: Congruence is baseline operational hygiene rather than differentiation by itself.

e94ecf5a6435ca1bd53cf497.applies_when: Structuring a collection, bundle selector, subscription tier page, or product comparison table where shoppers struggle to choose among options.
conditions: Absurd or dishonest reference prices and staged-looking tiers reduce credibility.

cadfc89e4c1d94d4d87d4d0a.applies_when: Improving a product launch, bundle, or cart incentive when shoppers understand the main item but hesitate over setup, selection, compatibility, or missing accessories.
conditions: Too many bonuses can hide the main product and make the offer harder to fulfill.

c8b36a7d028ee03d06b6855a.applies_when: Reviewing a proposed ecommerce offer change before it reaches paid traffic, email subscribers, or the storefront.
